Inside the loop, if x >= 5000000, z is incremented by 1, and in every iteration x is incremented by 1. Initially, before the loop starts at line 5, x is 0, y is 10000000, and z is 5000000. At the loop header (line 5), x starts at 0 and increments up to y. Thus, at line 5, 0 <= x <= 10000000. At the end of the loop execution when x reaches 10000000, the condition x < y becomes false. Since z starts at 5000000 and is incremented for each step where x >= 5000000 (which happens 5000000 times, from x = 5000000 to 9999999), z will also equal 10000000 at the termination point. Therefore, the assertion z == x holds at line 9.
